meaning: the whole year; all year round

senses.en: the whole year, all twelve months (全年都… 'all year round')
for the year as a whole, as a modifier before a noun, with or without 的 (全年的计划 'the plan for the year', 全年收入 'annual income')

examples.en: It's hot here all year round.
examples.analysis: 全年 is a time word, so it sits before the verb part, like 今天 or 明天. 都 'all, throughout' sums up the whole span that 全年 names; 全年都 + description is a common way to say 'all year round'.

examples.en: Is the plan for the whole year ready?
examples.analysis: Here 全年 + 的 describes 计划: 'the whole year's plan', a typical work topic. 做好 'do until it is done' + 了 + 吗 asks whether the job is finished.

examples.en: He didn't take a single day off all year.
examples.analysis: 全年 sets the time span before the verb. 请假 'ask for leave' splits around 过 and the amount: 请过一天假 'has taken a day of leave'. With 没 in front, 一天 means 'not even one day'.

collocations.en: no days off all year; open 365 days a year
the plan for the whole year

meaning: pronunciation; the way a character or word is read

senses.en: the pronunciation of a character or word (这个字的读音); for how well a person speaks, 发音 is more common

examples.en: This character has two pronunciations.
examples.analysis: 读音 is the object of 有: 有两个读音 'has two readings'. Before a measure word, 'two' is normally 两, not 二, and 个 counts the readings. For such characters, the word they appear in decides the reading.

examples.zh: 那它在这个词里是什么读音？
examples.en: So how is it pronounced in this word?
examples.analysis: 那 'then, so' opens a follow-up question, and 它 'it' points back to a character already mentioned. 什么读音 'which pronunciation' asks which reading applies 在这个词里 'in this word'.

examples.zh: 这个词的读音我老是记不住。
examples.en: I can never remember how this word is pronounced.
examples.analysis: 这个词的读音 'this word's pronunciation' comes first as the topic, then the subject 我. 记不住 'can't keep it in memory' puts 不 inside 记住, and 老是 'all the time, again and again' adds a note of frustration.

related.en: pronunciation, how a person sounds words

meaning: intermediate; middle-level

senses.en: intermediate (of a course, class, level or exam): 中级班, 中级水平
middle-ranking (of a professional grade or title): 中级职称

examples.en: I'm taking an intermediate Chinese class.
examples.analysis: 中级 sits right before 汉语课 and labels its level, like 'intermediate' in English. 上课 'attend class' opens up around the description: 上 + 中级汉语 + 课. 在 before the verb marks something ongoing.

examples.en: What time does the intermediate class start?
examples.analysis: 中级班 'the intermediate class': 中级 labels 班 directly, with no 的. It names a level rather than a quality, so it is not used with 很. 几点 + verb asks for a clock time, here when 上课 'class begins'.

examples.en: I'm not at intermediate level yet.
examples.analysis: 中级水平 'intermediate level' is what 到 'reach' points to. 还不到 'not yet reaching' says you are below that level for now.

meaning: Western medicine; a doctor of Western medicine

senses.en: Western (biomedical) medicine, as opposed to 中医 'Chinese medicine'
a doctor trained in Western medicine

measure.note: 一个西医 'a Western-medicine doctor'; 位 is more polite

examples.en: I'm a doctor of Western medicine, not Chinese medicine.
examples.analysis: Here 西医 names a person: 是西医 'am a Western-medicine doctor'. 不是中医 then rules out the other kind of doctor. 西医 and 中医 are the usual pair for this distinction.

examples.zh: 你生病了看西医还是中医？
examples.en: When you're ill, do you see a Western doctor or a Chinese medicine doctor?
examples.analysis: 看西医 'see a Western-medicine doctor' uses the 看 of 看病 'see a doctor', i.e. 'go to for treatment'. 还是 'or' joins the two choices in a question. 生病了 at the front sets the condition, 'once you are ill'.

examples.en: My grandma doesn't really trust Western medicine.
examples.analysis: 西医 here is the system, not a person: it is the object of 相信 'believe in, trust'. 不太 'not very' softens the statement; plain 不相信 would sound flatter and more absolute.

collocations.en: see a doctor of Western medicine

related.en: traditional Chinese medicine; a TCM doctor

meaning: traditional Chinese medicine; a doctor of Chinese medicine

senses.en: traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) as a system or a hospital department
a doctor of Chinese medicine (看中医 'see a TCM doctor')

measure.note: 一个老中医 'a seasoned TCM doctor'; 位 is more polite

examples.en: I'd like to go and see a Chinese medicine doctor.
examples.analysis: 看中医 'see a TCM doctor' uses the same 看 as 看病 'see a doctor'. 去 + verb means 'go and do', and 想 in front makes it a wish or a plan.

examples.en: The Chinese medicine doctor told me to drink less cold stuff.
examples.analysis: 中医 is the person here, the subject. 让 + person + action = 'have someone do', here as advice: 少喝 'drink less'. 凉的 'cool or chilled ones' drops the noun; after 喝 it means cold drinks. 凉 'cool, not warm' is common for food and drink, and so are 冷 and 冰 (冷水, 冰水).

examples.en: Does your hospital offer Chinese medicine?
examples.analysis: 中医 here means TCM as a service, a department or its doctors: 有中医吗 'is there Chinese medicine?'. 你们医院 'your hospital' takes no 的, which is normal before an organization someone belongs to.

collocations.en: see a doctor of Chinese medicine
a hospital of traditional Chinese medicine

meaning: overcast day; cloudy, grey weather

senses.en: an overcast day; grey weather with the sky covered, or nearly covered, by cloud

examples.en: It's overcast today, and a bit cold.
examples.analysis: 今天阴天 'today, overcast': in casual talk a weather noun like 阴天 can follow a time word directly, with no 是. 有点儿 + adjective 'a bit…', often for something mildly unwelcome, like 冷 here.

examples.en: Will tomorrow be sunny or overcast?
examples.analysis: Here 是 links 明天 to the two choices, joined by 还是 'or' in a question. 晴天 'sunny day' and 阴天 'overcast day' are a common pair of opposites in weather talk.

examples.en: When it's overcast, I don't feel like going out.
examples.analysis: 阴天 at the front sets the situation, 'on grey days', the way a time word would. 不想 'don't feel like' + 出门 'go out of the house'. The line states a general habit, so it needs no 了.

meaning: before long; in no time; soon after

senses.en: a short while later; usually tells what happened next, paired with 就 (不一会儿就…)

examples.zh: 孩子不一会儿就睡着了。
examples.en: The kid fell asleep in no time.
examples.analysis: 不一会儿 goes before the verb and says how little time passed. It usually pairs with 就 'then, already', which stresses that the next event came quickly. 睡着 'fall asleep' + 了 marks the change.

examples.zh: 我刚到，不一会儿就下雨了。
examples.en: I'd only just arrived, and before long it started to rain.
examples.analysis: Two events in a row: 刚到 'had just arrived', then 不一会儿就 'soon after'. Here 不一会儿 opens the second clause and links the two in time. 下雨了 'it started raining', with 了 for the new situation.

examples.zh: 他说去买水，不一会儿就回来了。
examples.en: He said he was going to buy water, and he was back in no time.
examples.analysis: 不一会儿 opens the second clause: first 他说去买水 'he said he'd go and buy water', then 不一会儿就回来了 'was back very soon'. 就 stresses how fast it happened, and 了 marks the completed return. Telling what happened next like this is the word's typical use.

collocations.en: in no time at all (不一会儿工夫就…)

related.en: a little while; in a moment (often about the future)

meaning: international student; a student studying abroad

senses.en: a foreign student, e.g. a foreigner studying in China
a student who has gone abroad to study (中国留学生 'Chinese students abroad')

measure.note: 一个留学生; 位 is more polite

examples.zh: 他是从越南来的留学生。
examples.en: He's an international student from Vietnam.
examples.analysis: 从越南来的 'who came from Vietnam' is a whole phrase + 的, placed before 留学生 to describe it. Said in China, 留学生 on its own usually means a foreign student studying there.

examples.zh: 你们学校有多少留学生？
examples.en: How many international students are there at your school?
examples.analysis: 有多少 + noun asks 'how many … are there'. 多少 can go straight before the noun with no measure word, as here. 你们学校 'your school' takes no 的, normal before an organization.

examples.zh: 我们班一个留学生也没有。
examples.en: There isn't a single international student in our class.
examples.analysis: 一个 + noun + 也没有 = 'not a single one': the object 一个留学生 moves before the verb for emphasis, and 也 strengthens the negative. 我们班 'our class' is the place being described.

meaning: Western food; a Western-style meal

senses.en: Western-style food or meals (steak, pasta, bread…), as opposed to 中餐 'Chinese food'

measure.note: 吃一顿西餐 'have a Western meal'; 份 for one portion or set

examples.zh: 今天晚上我们吃西餐吧。
examples.en: Let's have Western food tonight.
examples.analysis: 西餐 is the object of 吃. 吧 at the end turns the statement into a suggestion, 'let's…'. The time 今天晚上 'this evening' comes first, before the subject 我们.

examples.en: Is there any good Western food around here?
examples.analysis: 有 + noun + 吗 asks whether something can be found here. 好吃的 'tasty' is joined to 西餐 by 的, so the question is about good Western food, not just any.

examples.en: Western food doesn't fill me up.
examples.analysis: 西餐 comes first as the topic, then the subject 我. 吃不饱 puts 不 between the verb 吃 'eat' and the result 饱 'full': you can eat it, but you can't end up full.

meaning: the Spring Festival; Chinese (Lunar) New Year

senses.en: the Spring Festival, Chinese New Year: the first day of the lunar year and the holiday around it

examples.en: Are you going home for Chinese New Year?
examples.analysis: 春节 opens the question as a time word, 'at the Spring Festival'. 回家 'go home' is the trip many people make for the holiday, to be with family. 吗 turns it into a yes/no question.

examples.en: Plane tickets are expensive before Chinese New Year.
examples.analysis: 春节前 'before the Spring Festival': 前 'before' comes after the event it refers to, the reverse of English. 很 is unstressed here, so 'are expensive' fits; bare 机票贵 would sound like a contrast with something else.

examples.en: I'm not going back for Chinese New Year this year.
examples.analysis: 今年春节 'this year's Spring Festival' is the time topic. 不 + verb + 了 announces a change of plan: 'I've decided not to go back'. 回去 'go back there' points away from where the speaker is now.

collocations.en: the Spring Festival Gala on TV

meaning: exam candidate; test-taker

senses.en: a candidate sitting an exam, especially a big formal one (an entrance exam, the HSK)

measure.note: 一个考生; 名 (míng) in official counts

examples.en: Candidates, please line up over here.
examples.analysis: 考生 at the front addresses the listeners, the way staff speak outside an exam room. 请 + verb is a polite instruction, and 到这边 'come to this side' says where to go before 排队 'line up'.

examples.en: Are there a lot of candidates this year?
examples.analysis: Adjective + 不 + adjective, 多不多, asks a yes/no question without 吗. 今年的考生 'this year's candidates' is the subject, and 多 'many' is the predicate, with no verb 'to be'.

examples.zh: 考生不可以带手机进去。
examples.en: Candidates may not take their phones in.
examples.analysis: 不可以 'may not' states a rule, about permission rather than ability. 带 + thing + 进去 'take something in (there)': the object sits between the verb and the direction word.

collocations.en: candidates for the national university entrance exam

meaning: primary and secondary schools

senses.en: primary and secondary schools together, i.e. school from primary up to senior secondary (not kindergarten, not university): 中小学老师, 中小学生

examples.zh: 现在中小学的作业太多了。
examples.en: Primary and secondary schools give too much homework these days.
examples.analysis: 中小学 + 的 + 作业 'the homework of primary and secondary schools'. 太 + adjective + 了 = 'too…', a complaint. 现在 'nowadays' at the front frames it as a comment on how things are now.

examples.en: What date do primary and secondary schools start the new term?
examples.analysis: 中小学 is the subject, covering primary and secondary schools together. 几号 asks for a date in the month, and 开学 means 'school starts (for a new term)'. No 吗 is needed, since 几 already makes it a question.

examples.zh: 这儿的中小学下午四点就放学。
examples.en: Primary and secondary schools here let out as early as 4 p.m.
examples.analysis: 这儿的中小学 'the primary and secondary schools here' is the subject. 就 after a time means 'as early as, already then', so the speaker finds four o'clock early. 放学 'school lets out'.

meaning: not very; not quite; not really

senses.en: not very, not too (不太 + adjective): 不太好 'not very good'
not really, not quite (不太 + verb of liking or knowing): 不太明白

examples.en: I'm not feeling very well today.
examples.analysis: 不太 + adjective 'not very': 不太舒服 is the usual soft way to say you feel unwell, gentler than 不舒服. Mind the order: 太不舒服了 would mean 'really uncomfortable, really unwell'.

examples.en: Sorry, I don't quite understand.
examples.analysis: Before a verb of knowing or understanding, 不太 means 'not quite, not fully'. 不太明白 is softer than 不明白: you may have got part of it, or you are just being polite. Either way it invites the other person to explain again.

examples.en: Does he seem a bit unhappy?
examples.analysis: 是不是 + statement asks 'is it the case that…?', checking a guess. 不太高兴 'not very happy' is a gentle way to say someone seems unhappy or annoyed.

collocations.en: not very good; not a good idea

meaning: new word (in a lesson); unfamiliar word

senses.en: a new word in a lesson or text, one you have not learned yet

examples.en: What does this new word mean?
examples.analysis: Noun + 什么意思 asks 'what does … mean?'; casual speech often leaves out 是 here. 这个生词 'this new word' is one you are meeting for the first time in a text or lesson.

examples.en: I memorize ten new words a day.
examples.analysis: 一天 'a day, per day' before the verb gives the rate, so no word for 'every' is needed. 记 'commit to memory' takes 十个生词 as its object, counted with 个.

examples.en: I haven't reviewed these new words yet.
examples.analysis: 这些生词 'these new words' comes first as the topic, before the subject 我. 还没 + verb 'not yet': 没 for an action that hasn't happened, 还 for 'so far, still'.

meaning: not necessarily; not sure (yet); maybe not

senses.en: not necessarily, not certain to (不一定 + adjective or verb): 贵的不一定好
used alone as a reply: 'not sure yet', 'it depends'

examples.en: Expensive doesn't necessarily mean good.
examples.analysis: 贵的 'the expensive ones' is the subject, with the noun dropped. 不一定 goes before the predicate 好 and denies that one guarantees the other: some expensive things are good, some are not.

examples.en: He may or may not come tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 不一定 + verb 'not certain to': 不一定来 leaves the outcome open, unlike 不来 'won't come'. It sits after the subject and the time word, in the usual adverb slot before the verb.

examples.en: Not sure yet; it depends on the weather.
examples.analysis: Used alone, 不一定 is a reply: 'it may or may not happen'. 还 'still, as of now' adds 'yet'. 看 + noun 'depends on…' names the deciding factor, and 吧 softens the answer.

related.en: maybe; possibly (不一定来 'may or may not come'; 可能不来 'may not come')

meaning: text message (SMS)

senses.en: a text message sent over the phone network (SMS), e.g. from a friend or a bank

examples.en: Text me when you get there.
examples.analysis: 发短信 'send a text'; 给我 before the verb marks who gets it. 个 is a casual short form of 一个 and replaces the usual measure 条 here (发个短信), which makes the request sound light. 到了 at the front means 'once you've arrived'.

examples.en: Did you get my text?
examples.analysis: 收到 'receive' + 了 + 吗 asks whether something has arrived, with 我的短信 'my text' as the object in between. 收到 is the normal verb for getting messages, letters and parcels.

examples.zh: 银行的短信我一般不看。
examples.en: I usually don't read texts from the bank.
examples.analysis: 银行的短信 'texts from the bank' is the topic, moved to the front. 一般 'usually, as a rule' + 不 + verb describes a habit, so it takes 不, not 没.

meaning: cloudy (in weather reports); cloudy with some sun

senses.en: cloudy weather with some breaks of sun; a forecast term between 晴 'sunny' and 阴 'overcast'

examples.en: Tomorrow will be cloudy, with no rain.
examples.analysis: 多云 follows the time word directly, as in a weather forecast: 明天多云 'tomorrow, cloudy'. 不下雨 adds that it won't rain; 不 also works for predictions about the future.

examples.en: Will it be cloudy the day after tomorrow too?
examples.analysis: Here 是 links 后天 to 多云, and 也 'also' shows the speaker already knows another day is cloudy. Casual speech can also drop 是: 后天也多云吗？

examples.zh: 多云的话，我们去爬山吧。
examples.en: If it's cloudy, let's go hiking.
examples.analysis: …的话 'if' closes the condition: 多云的话 'if it's cloudy'. The speaker treats cloudy weather as good enough for a trip to 爬山 'go hiking'. 吧 makes the second part a suggestion.

meaning: bus

senses.en: a public bus; the full name (everyday speech more often says 公交车 or 公交, but 公共汽车 is also common)

measure.note: 一辆公共汽车; 路 for the route number: 3路公共汽车 'the No. 3 bus'

examples.en: I take the bus to work.
examples.analysis: 坐 'ride, travel by' is the verb for buses, trains and planes. Two verb phrases in a row, 坐公共汽车 + 上班, mean 'go to work by bus': the means comes first, then the purpose.

examples.zh: 这儿有去机场的公共汽车吗？
examples.en: Is there a bus to the airport from here?
examples.analysis: 去机场的 'that goes to the airport' describes the bus: a whole phrase + 的 comes before the noun. 这儿有…吗 asks whether something can be found here.

examples.zh: 这么晚了，没有公共汽车了。
examples.en: It's so late, there are no more buses.
examples.analysis: 没有…了 'there aren't any … anymore': the final 了 marks the change from 'there were buses' to 'there are none now'. 这么晚了 'it's this late now' gives the reason.

related.en: bus; the more common word in speech

meaning: (city) bus

senses.en: a city bus; the everyday word, often shortened to 公交

examples.en: The bus is here, hurry up!
examples.analysis: 公交车 is the subject; 来了 'has come', with 了 for something that has just happened. 快点儿 'quicker' on its own is a common way to say 'hurry up'.

examples.zh: 我们坐公交车去还是打车？
examples.en: Shall we take the bus or get a taxi?
examples.analysis: 还是 'or' offers two choices in a question: 坐公交车去 'go by bus' or 打车 'take a taxi'. 坐 is the verb for riding a bus, as in 坐地铁 'take the subway'.

examples.zh: 公交车上人太多了，我不想坐。
examples.en: The bus is too crowded, I don't want to take it.
examples.analysis: 公交车上 'on the bus': 上 after a place or thing gives 'on/in' that thing. 人太多了 'too many people' is the reason, and 不想坐 'don't want to ride' drops the object, which is clear from context.

related.en: bus; the full, more formal name

meaning: picture; drawing; painting

senses.en: a picture, drawing or painting; 画儿 with -儿 is the northern spoken form of the noun 画

measure.note: 一张画儿 'a picture'; 幅 (fú) is more formal

examples.en: This is a picture my daughter drew.
examples.analysis: Two 画 here: 画 'draw' is the verb inside 我女儿画的 'that my daughter drew', and 画儿 'picture' is the noun it describes. The -儿 ending goes on the noun; the verb 画 does not take it.

examples.en: Who painted the picture on the wall?
examples.analysis: 墙上的画儿 'the picture on the wall': place + 上 + 的 describes the noun. 是谁画的 uses 是…的 to ask about a detail of something already done, here who did it.

examples.en: I can't draw.
examples.analysis: 画画儿 'draw pictures' is the verb 画 + the noun 画儿, the usual northern way to say 'to draw' (many speakers say plain 画画). 不会 'can't' is about a learned skill, not permission or a single occasion.
